columnPool.label: Route: Fen Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Fen Line route

columnPool.label: Route: Elizabeth Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Elizabeth Line route
columnPool.hint: The cross-London route from Reading and Heathrow in the west through central London to Shenfield and Abbey Wood in the east - opened in 2022, London's newest railway.

columnPool.label: Route: Northern City Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Northern City Line route
columnPool.hint: The tunnel linking Moorgate to Finsbury Park, built for London Underground but now run as part of the Great Northern suburban network - originally planned as part of the Northern line's unbuilt 'Northern Heights' expansion.

columnPool.label: Route: Marston Vale Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Marston Vale Line route
columnPool.hint: The rural cross-country branch from Bedford via Ridgmont and Woburn Sands to Bletchley, running through the Marston Vale.

columnPool.label: Route: Lioness Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Lioness Line route
columnPool.hint: The London Overground route from Euston to Watford Junction via Wembley - renamed in 2024 to honour the England women's football team following their 2022 Euros victory.

columnPool.label: Route: Northern Heights
columnPool.display: Is part of the Northern Heights route
columnPool.hint: The Great Northern suburban branches north of London (towards Alexandra Palace, Hertford and Welwyn) that were originally slated for absorption into the London Underground's Northern line under a 1930s expansion plan, abandoned after the Second World War.

columnPool.label: Route: West Coast Main Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the West Coast Main Line route
columnPool.hint: The historic trunk route from London Euston to Glasgow via Rugby, Stafford, Crewe and Preston - Britain's busiest mixed-traffic main line.

columnPool.label: Route: Abbey Line
